dedupe_keys.name: gridpath india long term 2020 2050 power system planning model data

description: This data set holds the full inputs for GridPath-India, a capacity expansion model of India's electricity system built on the open-source GridPath platform. It was published on Dryad by Guillermo Terrén-Serrano, Ranjit Deshmukh, Srihari Dukkipati, Measrainsey Meng, Shradhey Prasad, Ana Mileva and Ashwin Gambhir, to make long-term Indian planning studies reproducible. The model has 34 load zones with interstate transmission and optimises generation, storage and transmission investment and operation from 2020 to 2050 using two representative days per month at hourly resolution. Inputs cover existing, planned and candidate generation and storage projects, more than 1,300 candidate wind and solar sites with hourly capacity factors from ERA5 and the NSRDB bias-corrected to the Global Wind Atlas and to reported state generation, state coal captive capacity, technology cost trajectories for batteries, pumped hydro, hydrogen, thermal, solar and wind, two sets of hourly demand projections, and scenarios for transmission, portfolios, reliability and policy targets. Coverage is India. Files are CSV archives, about 253 MB, downloadable from Dryad (version 6, January 2026) under CC0 at no cost. Caveats: representative days simplify operations, and some costs are adapted from US and international sources. Simulation uses are capacity expansion and policy scenarios for India.
